message.content:
Review the diff below for code REUSE opportunities. The work added "ROI kanata logging" to a hybrid QEMU+vsim simulator: a new vsim `--kanata-roi` CLI flag that auto-derives a single-shot pipeline-viewer window from the resume PC + a unique exit PC, plus hsim/e2e.sh wiring to forward `--kanata`/`--objdump` to vsim.

For each newly added function or inline block, search the repo for existing utilities that could replace it. Common reuse hotspots:

- `verilator/src/utils/`, `verilator/src/hybrid/` for vsim helpers
- `tests/lib/`, `tests/hsim/` for shared test helpers
- The Python driver `hsim` (around lines 1-300) for argv/env handling utilities
- `tests/e2e.sh` for existing argv-array conventions (`VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(...)`)

Specifically check whether:
1. `derive_roi_kanata_gate()` (verilator/src/hybrid/kanata_roi.hpp) duplicates any existing PC-derivation logic. Cross-check `enable_hybrid_handoff` in `verilator/src/simulator.hpp` which builds the same CsrTrigger.
2. `pcs_of_kind()` in csr_trigger.hpp duplicates any existing scan in CsrTrigger or sibling triggers (icount_trigger.hpp).
3. The bash awk-extraction of csrwi PCs in tests/hsim/test_hsim_kanata.sh duplicates anything in `tests/lib/` (roi.sh, paths.sh, log.sh).
4. The Python `Path(args.kanata).resolve()` env-export pattern in hsim has a sibling utility.
5. The `--kanata-roi` validation cascade in main.cpp could share code with the existing `--kanata-loop-*` validation cascade just above it (lines 400-420 of src/main.cpp).
6. The HandoffController `trigger()` const accessor I added: is there a sibling pattern already?

REPORT ONLY: list each finding as `file:line - issue - suggested existing utility - why this is reuse, not equivalent code`. Skip findings that turn out to be unique or where the existing utility's semantics differ. Under 400 words.

=== FULL DIFF ===

# verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp (modified)
Added at the end of the public section of class CsrTrigger:
```cpp
  // Collect every recorded PC whose hit matches `kind`. The result is sorted
  // ascending so callers (e.g. the ROI kanata-gate derivation) get a stable
  // order regardless of hash-map iteration order.
  auto pcs_of_kind(hybrid_handoff_kind kind) const -> std::vector<uint64_t>
  {
    std::vector<uint64_t> pcs;
    pcs.reserve(hits_.size());
    for (const auto& [pc, hit]: hits_)
      if (hit.kind == kind) pcs.push_back(pc);
    std::sort(pcs.begin(), pcs.end());
    return pcs;
  }
```
Also added `#include <algorithm>` and `#include <vector>`.

# verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp (modified)
Added after set_passthrough_input():
```cpp
  // Read-only view of the underlying trigger. Used by the ROI kanata-gate
  // derivation, which needs to read scanned EXIT PCs without consuming them.
  auto trigger() const -> const Trigger& { return trigger_; }
```

# verilator/src/hybrid/kanata_roi.hpp (NEW)
Pure helper, ~58 lines. derive_roi_kanata_gate(trigger, resume_pc, optional<explicit_exit_pc>) -> RoiKanataGate{start, end, skip=0, record=1}. csr-mode: picks unique HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT PC from trigger.pcs_of_kind(EXIT); 0 or >1 throws. pc-mode: uses explicit_exit_pc.

# verilator/src/simulator.hpp (modified)
Added new method enable_kanata_roi(filename, objdump_file, optional<explicit_exit_pc>): validates hybrid_input_state_ + hybrid_handoff_ are set, calls derive_roi_kanata_gate, wraps result in kanata::LoopGate, calls trace_.enable_kanata.

# verilator/src/main.cpp (modified)
- New `--kanata-roi` longflag
- New validation block (~20 lines) before enable_kanata: requires --kanata, mutually exclusive with --kanata-loop-* (loop_gate set), --clarity, --hybrid-icount; requires --resume-from-qemu.
- Skips early enable_kanata when --kanata-roi is set; calls sim.enable_kanata_roi after enable_hybrid_handoff instead.

# hsim (Python, modified)
- `--kanata FILE`, `--objdump FILE` argparse args on `run` subcommand
- Validation in cmd_run: rejects with rc=2 if mode not in (csr, pc); rejects --objdump without --kanata
- _run_via_e2e: exports KANATA_FILE=Path(args.kanata).resolve(), OBJDUMP_FILE=Path(args.objdump).resolve()

# tests/e2e.sh (modified)
Built VSIM_KANATA_ARGS array (similar to existing VSIM_TRIG_ARGS):
```bash
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi
```
And appended to the vsim invocation.

# tests/hsim/test_hsim_kanata.sh (NEW)
Bash smoke test. Sources tests/lib/log.sh for fail/ok. Sources config.env if HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN unset. Extracts csrwi PCs via objdump+awk for pc-mode case.

# verilator/tests/hybrid/csr_trigger.test.cpp / kanata_roi.test.cpp / docs/USER_GUIDE.md / kanata_roi.md
Tests and docs for the above.

2	// HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT once the per-hart counter reaches the configured target.
3	// Pure logic: no SystemC, no DMI bus.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
3	#
4	# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
5	# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
6	# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
7	# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
8	# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.
9	
10	# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
11	#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
12	#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
13	# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
14	# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
15	resolve_pc() {
16	  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
17	  case "$boundary" in

25	#   each against <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare
26	#   hex). Returns 1 and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if
27	#   either is unset or does not resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message.
28	roi_resolve_pair() {
29	  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
30	  local start="${ROI_START:-}"
31	  local end="${ROI_END:-}"
32	  if [ -z "$start" ] || [ -z "$end" ]; then
33	    echo "FAIL[$label]: ROI_START and ROI_END must both be set (0x address or symbol name)"
34	    return 1
35	  fi
36	  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
37	  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
38	  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
39	    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
40	    return 1
41	  fi
42	  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
43	    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
44	    return 1
45	  fi
46	  return 0
47	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end roundtrip harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim -> QEMU 2.
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   EXPECT_RC       Final exit code to assert (default 0).
13	#   TRIGGER_MODE    csr | pc (default csr).
14	#   ROI_START       pc mode REQUIRED. Switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol
15	#                   in $VSIM_ELF.
16	#   ROI_END         pc mode REQUIRED. Switch-out PC, same forms.
17	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
18	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
19	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
20	#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
21	
22	set -euo pipefail
23	
24	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
25	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
26	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"
27	
28	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
29	EXPECT_RC="${EXPECT_RC:-0}"
30	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
31	TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-csr}"
32	
33	hybrid_resolve_paths
34	
35	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
36	NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
37	
38	case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
39	  csr) ;;
40	  pc)
41	    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
42	      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
43	      exit 77
44	    fi
45	    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
46	    # ROI_START / ROI_END (env, both required) name the two switch PCs:
47	    # each is a 0x address or a symbol in $VSIM_ELF.
48	    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
49	    ;;
50	  *)
51	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use csr|pc)"
52	    exit 1
53	    ;;
54	esac
55	
56	# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
57	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
58	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
59	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
60	STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
61	SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
62	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
63	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
64	
65	PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
66	VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
67	if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
68	  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
69	  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
70	fi
71	
72	# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
73	# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
74	# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
75	VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
76	if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
77	  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
78	  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
79	    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
80	  fi
81	fi
82	
83	echo "[$FIXTURE 1/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
84	set +e
85	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
86	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
87	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
88	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
89	  -nographic \
90	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
91	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
92	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" >/dev/null 2>&1
93	QEMU1_RC=$?
94	set -e
95	
96	if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
97	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
98	  exit 1
99	fi
